slot.brief: Give a transition metal ion (e.g. Mn2+ or Cr3+ or Fe3+), ask for its d-electron configuration, count of unpaired electrons, and the spin-only moment in BM using √(n(n+2)).

stem: For an isolated gaseous $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion ($Z=27$), what are its $d$-electron configuration, number of unpaired electrons and spin-only magnetic moment, respectively?

verdicts.working: Co: [Ar] 3d⁷4s²; Co²⁺ loses the two 4s electrons, giving 3d⁷. Hund’s rule gives 3 unpaired electrons, so μ = √[3(3 + 2)] = √15 BM.

working:
$\text{Co}: [\text{Ar}]\,3d^7 4s^2$; remove the two $4s$ electrons for $\text{Co}^{2+}$.
$\text{Co}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]\,3d^7$.
Hund's rule gives $n=3$ unpaired electrons.
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3(5)}=\sqrt{15}\ \text{BM}$.

Independent check: Co: [Ar] 3d⁷4s²; Co²⁺ loses the two 4s electrons, giving 3d⁷. Hund’s rule gives 3 unpaired electrons, so μ = √[3(3 + 2)] = √15 BM.
solution:
Co has configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^7 4s^2$; removing the two $4s$ electrons gives $\text{Co}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^7$. Hund’s rule gives $n=3$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3(5)}=\sqrt{15}\ \text{BM}$$
